clue.text: Crest crowning bird

parts.note: crowning means at the top, so it gives top
the knot is a small wading bird

explanation.surface: A crest sits on top of some bird's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowning' looks like it describes the crest's position, but it supplies the first half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a tuft of hair or feathers on the crown of the head, the same thing as a crest.

clue.text: Storm split a party

parts.note: something split is torn
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A row divides a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling windstorm.

clue.text: Ruddy good portrait?

parts.note: ruddy reads as a mild British expletive praising the picture, but really means rosy-cheeked, a well person's complexion

explanation.surface: A really excellent painting of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' is British slang for 'bloody', an intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks the image of fitness has a ruddy glow, an image of wellbeing.

clue.text: Not far off being a serious accident

definitions.text: Not far off being a serious accident

parts.words: Not far off being a serious accident
parts.note: describes a narrow escape, an incident that very nearly became a disaster

explanation.surface: Something came close to being a bad crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape is called this, since the disaster came close but did not happen.

clue.text: It goes up over a redhead, a crown

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, so the word it reads backwards

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of red

explanation.surface: Something rises above a red-haired woman, a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns IT into TI. 'redhead' looks like a red-haired person but gives R, the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headband or coronet, a kind of crown.

clue.text: City bird takes the water

parts.note: a swan is a large water bird
the sea is the water in a general sense

explanation.surface: In some city a bird goes for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: SWANSEA is a city in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in Wales, a specific example of a city.

clue.text: Lotion used by star on television

parts.note: the sun is our star
the screen is a word for television

explanation.surface: A cream that a TV celebrity uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks like a celebrity, but it is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunscreen is a cream applied to skin to block ultraviolet rays.

clue.text: A long bone

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A lengthy bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to yearn. AITCH is the rump bone of beef, as in aitchbone.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the butcher's term for the rump bone of cattle, a cut of beef.

clue.text: One's conscience, nevertheless, does not have much to say

parts.note: still means nevertheless
small means little in amount
to voice is to say

explanation.surface: A person's conscience, despite everything, is fairly quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from the Bible (1 Kings 19), the inner voice of God or conscience.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical phrase for the quiet inner prompting of morality, an idiom for the moral sense.

clue.text: Punished a soldier taking limited edition

parts.note: a merc is a mercenary soldier
edition limited, or cut short, gives ED, its standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A soldier was disciplined for grabbing a collector's copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited edition' suggests a rare print run, but means the word edition shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To amerce is to punish with a fine, an archaic legal term for penalising.

clue.text: People opposed to the enemy are in a hurry

parts.note: a race is a people, an ethnic group
against means opposed to
time is proverbially the enemy, as in 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: A nation at war with its foe is pressed for time.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: to race against time is to hurry to meet a deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: To race against time is to rush to finish before a deadline, the idiom for being hurried.

clue.text: One in the majority

parts.note: majority here is the age of majority, legal grown-up status, not the larger part of a group

explanation.surface: Someone who sides with most people.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching one's majority means attaining legal age, so a person past it is a grown-up.

clue.text: One who is overfond of this drink

definitions.text: One who is overfond of this drink

parts.words: One who is overfond of this drink
parts.note: the description first names a person addicted to drink, and the same word also describes the drink itself, as in an intoxicating beverage

explanation.surface: Someone who likes a particular drink too much.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a person dependent on liquor and an adjective for a drink containing spirits.

clue.text: One time round the rose-garden, that is to say, in submission

indicators.note: round means the outer word encloses the others

parts.note: once means one time
a flower bed is where roses are grown
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is to say

explanation.surface: A single stroll around the rose-garden, as it were, by way of yielding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reads like a stroll around the garden but tells you to wrap one piece around the rest; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is compliance with authority, the act of yielding or submitting.

clue.text: Curl Anton developed during the night

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Anton had his hair curled overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal describes things happening or active at night.

clue.text: Pointed weapon

parts.note: the phrase looks like a noun, a sharp spear or similar, but read as a verb phrase it means having pointed a gun at a target

explanation.surface: A sharp weapon such as a spear or arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: To point a weapon at a target is to direct it there, the past tense of taking aim.

clue.text: Top of the shaft

parts.note: the shaft sounds like a mine or lift shaft, but is the shaft of an arrow, whose tip is its top

explanation.surface: The upper end of a mine shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrowhead is the pointed tip fixed to the front of an arrow.

clue.text: Obscure expeditionary force leaders in unstable ground

indicators.note: in means the leaders are placed inside the word for unstable ground

parts.note: a bog is soft, wet ground that will not bear weight

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of the words expeditionary and force

explanation.surface: An expeditionary force's commanders get lost in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' picks E and F; 'in' sets them inside BOG.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to cloud or confuse something, making it obscure.

clue.text: Army equipment that has been packed for the journey

definitions.meaning: an army's portable equipment and supplies on the march

definitions.text: that has been packed for the journey

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an army's movable supplies and a traveller's luggage.

clue.text: Against another lot giving voice

parts.note: contra is Latin for against, used in English as in pro and contra

indicators.note: another means a different version, so the letters of lot are given in another order

explanation.surface: Opposing a different group by speaking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' reads as 'a different group' in the surface, but tells you to put lot into a different order; 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice, a type of voice in music.

clue.text: Scrap there's no match for

parts.note: a scrap, or leftover piece, which is odd because it has no pair, rather than a fight no one can win

explanation.surface: A fight that nobody can win.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover piece or remnant, odd because unmatched.

clue.text: Lap-dog?

parts.note: not a pet that sits on a lap but a dog that runs laps around a racing track

explanation.surface: A small pampered pet that sits on its owner's knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyhounds are racing dogs that run laps of an oval track, hence a dog of laps.

clue.text: Ethel entered part as another lady

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the words Ethel entered is used

explanation.surface: Ethel came on stage playing a different woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' suggests a stage role but signals that the answer is part of 'Ethel entered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen is a woman's name, so a lady other than Ethel.

clue.text: It's a fact that mother's holding the second person in France

indicators.note: holding means the word for mother encloses the pronoun

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
tu is the French word for you, the second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A truth: mother is keeping hold of the other French person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the French pronoun inside the word for mother; 'It's' and 'that' are only links around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, one known item.

clue.text: Having given up voluntarily I left having had a flutter

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter I goes out of the longer word

parts.note: to waive a right is to give it up voluntarily

explanation.surface: Someone renounced something and walked out after a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a flutter' suggests a bet, but the flutter is of a hand or flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving is moving something to and fro, so a flag that fluttered was waved.

clue.text: At every point stations might be found

definitions.meaning: an idiom for throughout, in every respect
railway stations are situated at intervals on a railway route

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means everywhere or in every respect, and literally railway stations stand along a railway track.

clue.text: Coming from Athlone with volatile flammable substance

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and changeable, so the letters of the Irish town are rearranged

explanation.surface: A volatile substance that burns comes out of an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Athlone is a town in the Irish midlands. 'Volatile' also suits the definition, since this alcohol evaporates readily.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol is ethyl alcohol, a liquid fuel that burns readily.

clue.text: Dew reformed during fog in America

indicators.note: during means one thing takes place within another, so the rearranged letters go inside

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new shape, so the letters of dew are rearranged

explanation.surface: Moisture collects again in the foggy weather of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' asks for the letters of dew in a new order, and 'during' sets them inside the word for fog; 'in America' is a loose definition of a region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midwest is a large region of the United States, a place located in America.
